match_note: The first-round manuscript is a later revision than arXiv v1. Evidence: (1) R2 cites arXiv 2502.16700, posted after v1 (January 2025); (2) referees describe a Fig. 4 with a superfluid-stiffness red line in 4d, quantum-metric distributions in 4e/4f and a calculated superconducting correlation vs U in 4g, whereas v1 Fig. 4e/4f are dV/dI curves, the stiffness and red line are in Fig. 5d, and v1 has no quantum-metric calculation at all; (3) R3 says Supplementary Note 4 explains chemical-potential extraction, but v1 Supp. Note 4 is cascade transitions; (4) the 'quantum metric hot spots' framing and published title are absent from v1 (v1 title: 'Probing electric field tunable multiband superconductivity in alternating twisted quadralayer graphene'); (5) line numbers shift (the N-2 sentence is line 48 for R3, near line 43 in v1). The experimental data, the 50 meV bandwidth, vn ~ 1700 m/s, the pairing-density definition, the 10/3 CDW inference and the n0 procedure are all already in v1; the theory section was added after v1.

concerns.quote: the paper in terms of new data does not seem to go beyond what was reported in Refs. 10 and 11.
concerns.summary: The superconductivity data and flat vs Dirac band analysis largely repeat prior ATQG/ATMG work (Refs. 10, 11; Nat. Mater. 2022; arXiv 2502.16700) and Figs. 3-4 resemble twisted bilayer and trilayer results, so the authors must state what is new.

concerns.quote: Also, the theory interpretation is heavily inspired by Ref. 45.
concerns.summary: The quantum-metric interpretation is largely borrowed from an earlier theory paper, limiting conceptual novelty.

concerns.quote: the connection is somewhat tenuous as the evidence is quite indirect, and there are many assumptions and inferences.
concerns.summary: The link between the superconducting data and quantum geometry rests on theory and assumptions, not direct experimental evidence, and alternative mechanisms are not discussed or ruled out.

concerns.quote: Does this definition assume that the pairing only comes from the flat carriers, and if so, is there a good reason for doing this?
concerns.summary: Defining the pairing density as |nu_flat - 2| ignores the non-negligible Dirac carrier density, which would change kF and the extracted coupling strength.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: Are there other possible explanations of the second 'critical density' around line 191 (which was needed to get v_n)?
concerns.summary: The higher critical current used to extract the flat-band velocity vn may have other origins than the assumed velocity saturation at the correlated gap.

concerns.quote: The estimation of the conventional contribution to the superfluid stiffness relies on a lot of assumptions. ... What happens if we use the effective velocity of the Dirac carriers instead?
concerns.summary: The conventional superfluid stiffness baseline depends on using the flat-band vn; using the Dirac velocity would make it much larger and could erase the claimed geometric excess.

concerns.quote: Why is the conventional contribution (red line) in Fig 4d flat vs U? I thought the band structure would evolve with U
concerns.summary: The conventional stiffness reference is drawn constant in displacement field even though the bands (and a claimed vHS) evolve with U and are interaction-broadened.

concerns.quote: How can the flat band be significantly broadened and yet extremely flat within the same transport study?
concerns.summary: The ~50 meV interaction-broadened bandwidth from Landau fans appears to contradict the 'extremely flat' vn ~ 1700 m/s from critical currents.

concerns.quote: I could not understand the chemical potential extraction technique in lines 119-131 after reading it several times.
concerns.summary: The chemical-potential extraction from Landau-level trajectories (mu_1 and mu_2 intersecting in Fig. 2d) is unclear and needs explanation, perhaps a schematic.

concerns.quote: What's the difference between fig 4e and 4f? Do they correspond to quantum metric distributions at different displacement fields?
concerns.summary: The two quantum-metric panels are not distinguished in the caption, and R2 asks to see the quantum metric at several U.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: Can the authors provide some intuition for why hybridization between flat bands and Dirac bands enhances quantum metric?
concerns.summary: The mechanism by which flat/Dirac hybridization enhances the quantum metric is not explained.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: provide an intuitive/qualitative explanation for the eventual decrease of the calculated superconducting correlation at large U in Fig 4g?
concerns.summary: Why the calculated pair correlation falls at large displacement field is not explained.

concerns.quote: Sometimes the counting of bands in the text is inconsistent.
concerns.summary: Statements like 'N - 2 dispersive bands' and 'the flat band' miscount bands; there are 2(N-2) dispersive bands (N-2 low-energy Dirac cones) and two flat bands.

concerns.quote: do the authors have independent evidence for a charge density wave state at 10/3?
concerns.summary: The inferred charge density wave at filling 10/3 lacks independent support such as a zero-field resistive feature.

concerns.quote: The Hartree effect of the relative shift of flat and Dirac carriers has been theoretically explored previously in various alternating twist multilayer platforms.
concerns.summary: Prior theory on Hartree-driven relative shifts of flat and Dirac bands (including ATQG) should be cited.

concerns.quote: Is it clear that there really is a proper insulator at exactly four carriers per moire unit cell?
concerns.summary: Extracting n0 from a full-filling resistance peak at finite U is questionable if flat and Dirac bands still overlap, so there may be no true insulator at full filling.

later_concerns.quote: Like I mentioned in the initial review, I think novelty for this paper is a weak point but I can recommend its publication at this stage.
later_concerns.summary: R2 still regards novelty as weak but recommends publication; R1 and R3 are fully satisfied.

first_round.quote: On the technical level, I don't have any significant concerns; the paper is worth publishing. However, I am unsure whether Nature Communications is the correct journal
I can in principle recommend publication provided that the authors can address my questions below. However, I want to point out that the manuscript is relatively weak in terms of novelty.
I would suggest publication in Nature Communications if the authors address the following comments

recommendations.note: No transfer from another journal is indicated; Version 0 is the first round. No referee co-signed another's report. R2's first-round report appears as an attachment at the end of the file; the in-text remark says only 'See the attached report.' R1 is borderline: they find the paper technically sound and worth publishing but question its novelty and fit for the journal. They only ask the authors to highlight novelty, so this was read as minor revision rather than reject. R3 is borderline between minor and major revision: they call the quantum-geometry link 'somewhat tenuous' and ask for clearer explanation and a more critical discussion of assumptions and alternative mechanisms. These requests involve rewriting and discussion, not new data, and R3 frames them as conditions for publication, so this was read as minor revision. All three recommended publication in round 2.
recommendations.label: clean
